newsitem.title: GERMANY: Lufthansa promises more money to bumped passengers.
newsitem.headline: Lufthansa promises more money to bumped passengers.

text.p: German airline Deutsche Lufthansa AG plans to increase the compensation that it pays to passengers who have been bumped from overbooked flights, the airline said on Saturday.
Beginning next Tuesday, at the height of Germany's summer holiday period, Lufthansa will offer passengers coupons valued at 1,200 marks or a cash refund of 600 marks," a Lufthansa spokesman said.
Until now Lufthansa had offered bumped passengers coupons worth 900 marks or a lump sum of 600 marks in cash.
Stranded passengers can use coupons to purchase another airline ticket or exchange them for goods sold aboard Lufthansa flights or in Lufthansa stores the airline said.
Nearly eight in every 10,000 Lufthansa passengers are bumped off overbooked flights, an airline spokesman said, noting the airline improves its capacity utilisation by overbooking flights.
Although the airline spends some 15 million marks in compensation every year this is offset by some 230 million marks in additional sales achieved by overbooking, the spokesman said.
